Blood Testament Chapter 3 Patch Notes
11月3日
\[Patch Introduction]
\[Highlights]
New Weapon: Lancaster
A four barreled, medium ammo pistol with a rotating firing pin which allows for a high fire rate. Favored by Hunters on safari as a self-defense weapon due to its superior reliability and stopping power. Opening the break-action will always eject all rounds.
Basic - 4/12
High Velocity - 4/8
Poison - 4/12
Can be dual-wielded.
New Variant: Lancaster Cleaver
A variant of the Lancaster with an under-barrel blade, changing its melee attacks to be similar to a Heavy Knife in both swing pattern and damage.
Basic - 4/12
High Velocity - 4/8
Poison - 4/12
Can be dual-wielded.
World
All Bileweaver Infested Compounds (new and Old) will have a chance to spawn in Chapter 3. There will be 5 compounds active per game.
Fair Play Follow Up
Players get a follow up notification when a player they reported was banned
Players get a Hunt Dollar refund when they get killed by a player who was banned
High ping queue (Temporary test in Europe for the duration of Chapter 3)
Players get matchmade into a separate queue if their ping is above a threshold. The goal is to reduce exposure to high-latency gameplay. Should they not be able to find a match, they rejoin the regular matchmaking queue.
\[Upcoming Updates]
New Community Event: “Reap the Harvest”
“Reap the Harvest” is a new Community Event that is planned to start later in Chapter 3. The Community Event will consist of 5 Stages, each offering a reward to the whole of the community. Players will progress the Community Event by earning Community Event Points which is done by completing objectives in matches.
Community Event Stage Rewards
Stage 1: 5K Hunt Dollars & 1K Event Points
Stage 2: Lancaster (New Weapon)
Stage 3: 10K Hunt Dollars & 2.5K Event Points
Stage 4: Lancaster Cleaver (New Weapon)
Stage 5: Random Legendary Skin

A Unique Masterpiece Undermined by Its Own Systems
Hunt: Showdown 1896 remains one of the most uniquely tense tactical shooters on PC, presenting an atmosphere and audio framework that no other game can match. However, your enjoyment of this brutal extraction shooter depends almost entirely on who you play with, as a frustrating matchmaking system and a severe lack of permanent game modes drag down an otherwise brilliant experience.
+------------------------------------+------------------------------------+
| The Good | The Bad |
+------------------------------------+------------------------------------+
| • Masterful PC gunplay & audio | • Wildly inconsistent matchmaking |
| • Highly rewarding team play | • Punishing, tedious solo experience|
| • Mechanically unique atmosphere | • Barely any permanent game modes |
+------------------------------------+------------------------------------+
The Friend Factor: Duo/Trio Brilliance vs. Solo Misery
On PC, where precision aiming elevates the stakes, Hunt is a masterpiece when played with a dedicated group of friends. Coordinating flanks, managing sound discipline, and executing dynamic pushes in duos or trios showcases the game at its absolute best.
Playing solo, however, feels like a completely different—and often miserable—game. While Crytek gives solo players certain trait advantages, going alone turns Hunt into an exhausting, hyper-passive waiting game. One wrong step means immediate death with zero room for error, pushing solo play into a tedious, ultra-stealth playstyle that strips away the dynamic fun of team firefights.
Horrible Matchmaking
The biggest barrier to enjoying the game consistently is its wildly erratic matchmaking system.
• On the Steam Community Forums, players frequently complain that the Matchmaking Rating (MMR) is fundamentally broken, regularly throwing lower-tier players or casual duos into lobbies with highly coordinated, max-rank sweat squads.
• People on Reddit emphasize that the game often prioritizes filling lobbies quickly over ensuring competitive balance, leaving average players feeling like cannon fodder for the upper echelons of the PC player base.
A Severe Lack of Game Modes
For a live-service game that has been running for years, Hunt’s lack of game modes is incredibly disappointing. The experience is essentially split into one main mode: Bounty Hunt. While Crytek occasionally introduces experimental, fast-paced modes like Bounty Clash during seasonal events to inject quick PvP action, these are typically time-limited.
Aside from the core extraction loop and the lesser-played Soul Survivor (a casual solo-only mode), there is nothing else permanently available. If you get tired of tracking clues and chasing the exact same boss tokens map after map, the game offers no permanent alternative playlists or sandbox variations to break up the repetition.
The Verdict
When Hunt: Showdown 1896 clicks—ideally while on Discord with two friends—it delivers a high-stakes, atmospheric rush that no other PC shooter can replicate. But if you are jumping in alone, relying on random teammates, or expecting a variety of ways to play, the game’s terrible MMR balance and stagnant mode selection make the Bayou a highly frustrating place to be.
